Topic: The Magic of the Central Limit Theorem (CLT)

Target audience: University students (Introductory Statistics)

Section: section_1 — The Hook: The Chaos of Individuals

Lecture lines:
Individual data points are often chaotic and unpredictable.
Consider a uniform distribution of squirrel jumps.
There is no clear pattern in the noise.

Planned animations:
Create 100 scattered dots (#FF9900) on a 1D line representing squirrel jumps.
Label the scatter plot 'Uniform Distribution: Individual Squirrels'.
Highlight that the distribution of jump lengths is chaotic and uneven.

Section: section_2 — The Prerequisite: Averages as Stabilizers

Lecture lines:
Averages act as powerful stabilizers for data.
Tracking a sample mean reduces extreme noise.
Repeated sampling reveals a hidden order.

Planned animations:
Group the squirrel jumps into smaller sets of 10.
Calculate the average jump distance for each set.
Show the averages stabilizing on a new, narrower number line.

Section: section_3 — The Reveal: Convergence to the Bell Curve

Lecture lines:
Chaotic data morphs into a Bell Curve.
As sample sizes grow, patterns emerge naturally.
This is the Central Limit Theorem revealed.
Order emerges directly from random fluctuations.
A perfect Normal Distribution finally forms.

Planned animations:
Start with the 'chaotic' scatter plot from section 1.
Animate the transition as sample size (n) increases from 1 to 30.
Morph the distribution into a smooth Bell Curve (#00CCFF).
Add a label: 'Normal Distribution: Sampling Mean'.
Highlight the peak of the curve to show the convergence point.

Section: section_4 — Key Properties & Constraints

Lecture lines:
Mean of sample means equals population mean.
Variance decreases as sample size grows.
Independence is essential for this convergence.

Planned animations:
Display the formula: μ_x̄ = μ (#FFFFFF).
Display the formula: σ_x̄ = σ / √n (#FFFFFF).
Visualize the variance shrinking as 'n' increases.

Section: section_5 — Application: Predicting the Future

Lecture lines:
Predict outcomes of large groups with confidence.
We move beyond knowing individual behaviors.
Statistical tools guarantee precise, predictable averages.

Planned animations:
Display a conveyor belt with cookie bags moving past a scanner.
Visualize the bell curve representing the weight of bags of 50.
Highlight the central area of the bell curve to show 'Acceptance Range'.

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            "Order emerges directly from random fluctuations.",
            "A perfect Normal Distribution finally forms."
        ])

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Predict outcomes of large groups with confidence.",
            "We move beyond knowing individual behaviors.",
            "Statistical tools guarantee precise, predictable averages."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: Predicting the Future", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Conveyor belt with cookie bags
        belt = Line(start=self.grid["F1"], end=self.grid["F6"], color=GRAY)
        self.add(belt)
        
        bags = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(3)])
        bags.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        bags.move_to(self.grid["E4"])
        self.add(bags)
        
        scanner = Square(side_length=0.8, color=RED).move_to(self.grid["D4"])
        self.add(scanner)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=1)
        self.play(bags.animate.shift(RIGHT * 2), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Bell curve representing weights
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 1, 0.5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-x**2), color=GREEN)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(curve, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight acceptance range
        highlight = axes.plot(lambda x: np.exp(-x**2), x_range=[-1, 1], color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(highlight, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeIn(highlight), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1)
